messages:
acme-inc: Hey team — since last night our prod k8s cluster (prod-us-east-1) intermittently fails to hit our private service endpoint svc.acme.internal. App sees 502/503s and our e2e tests are flaky. Repro: from pod: 

$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @127.0.0.53
10.2.3.25

Then sometimes it returns a public IP: 

$ dig +short svc.acme.internal @127.0.0.53
34.120.45.80

Happens ~1-3x an hour. Can you triage?

morgan (Support): Thanks — can you paste a full dig +trace and the output of cat /etc/resolv.conf from one of the failing pods? Also which VPC and whether you use node-local-dns? :eyes:

acme-inc: Sure — pod resolv.conf below and dig +trace (snips):

/etc/resolv.conf:
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options ndots:5

# dig +trace (shortened)
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> svc.acme.internal
;; global options: +cmd
;; Received 0 bytes; truncated
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; ANSWER SECTION:
svc.acme.internal.  300 IN A 10.2.3.25
;; but running again shows:
svc.acme.internal.  300 IN A 34.120.45.80

morgan (Support): Interesting — that pattern usually means queries are being answered by different DNS paths (VPC resolver vs. an external resolver). Do you have any egress/proxy rules that rewrite DNS or a corporate DNS forwarder?

acme-inc: We do have a corporate firewall / egress proxy. Kube nodes are supposed to only talk to the VPC resolver, but the infra team recently added a node-local-dns config to forward to an internal forwarder (10.10.10.10) for corporate names. I can run tcpdump if helpful.

taylor (SRE): Yes, tcpdump please. Also check that your AWS VPC Private Hosted Zone for svc.acme.internal is associated with the correct VPC(s) and that the VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) has private DNS enabled. If private DNS is disabled, clients may fall back to public records.

acme-inc: tcpdump from the pod (filtered):

14:12:01.123456 IP 10.2.1.5.56000 > 8.8.8.8.53: 12345+ A? svc.acme.internal. (40)
14:12:01.124000 IP 8.8.8.8.53 > 10.2.1.5.56000: 12345 1/0/0 A 34.120.45.80 (56)

Then at 14:12:45:
14:12:45.000111 IP 10.2.1.5.56001 > 10.2.2.53.53: 54321+ A? svc.acme.internal. (40)
14:12:45.000500 IP 10.2.2.53.53 > 10.2.1.5.56001: 54321 1/0/0 A 10.2.3.25 (56)

anya (Eng): That shows queries sometimes going to 8.8.8.8 (public DNS) and sometimes to the VPC resolver (10.2.2.53). So split-horizon responses are expected: Route53 private hosted zone returns private IPs, public DNS returns public IPs. The upstream choice is inconsistent. What's forwarding 127.0.0.53 -> 8.8.8.8?

kevin (Network): Checked our egress ACLs on the firewall — we had an allow rule that permits outbound to 8.8.8.8:53 for 'legacy metrics stack' and a higher-priority deny for 53 to all other external IPs, but we never added an explicit allow for the VPC resolver. i.e. nodes could reach 8.8.8.8 but not the VPC resolver IPs through the corporate perimeter. Here's the relevant snippet from the policy (redacted):

# firewall-policy (excerpt)
allow tcp/udp 10.2.0.0/16 -> 8.8.8.8:53  (legacy metrics)
deny  udp any -> 0.0.0.0/0:53  (block public DNS)
# Missing: allow 10.2.0.0/16 -> 10.2.2.53:53 (VPC resolver)

kevin (Network): So workflows that end up sending queries to 8.8.8.8 get public answers; ones that reach the VPC resolver get private answers. Node-local-dns had upstreams configured to the corporate forwarder which sometimes forwards to 8.8.8.8. That explains the intermittency.

morgan (Support): Ok we have a plausible root cause: inconsistent DNS forwarding due to egress allowlist + node-local-dns pointing at a corporate forwarder that sends some queries externally. Workarounds and steps below.

anya (Eng): Suggested immediate mitigations:
- Update node-local-dns upstreams to point only at the VPC resolver IP(s) (prevent forwarding to corporate forwarder).
- Ensure kubelet resolv.conf on nodes points to the node-local-dns (127.0.0.53) but node-local-dns must not forward to public resolvers.
- Short-term: add iptables DNAT on nodes to force queries for svc.acme.internal to VPC resolver (quick hack).

kevin (Network): Permanent remediation:
1) Update corporate egress policy to explicitly allow DNS (53 TCP/UDP) from the prod VPC IP range to the VPC resolver IP(s) and AWS resolver endpoints used by PrivateLink.
2) Block/deny direct egress to public resolvers like 8.8.8.8 for pods in prod VPC unless explicitly required.
3) Validate Private DNS enabled on the PrivateLink endpoint: aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-xxxx --private-dns-enabled

morgan (Support): Quick steps we applied for the customer (worked):
- Rolled node-local-dns config to upstream only 10.2.2.53 (VPC resolver).
- Restarted node-local-dns and dnsmasq on cluster nodes.
- Confirmed dig always returns 10.2.3.25 after change.

acme-inc: After the node-local-dns change + firewall update our e2e run is now green. Thanks team! :tada:

oncall-bot: Ticket #INC-2026-981 created, severity S2. Assigned to kevin (Network) for permanent policy update.

morgan (Support): Follow-ups: we recommend you run a short audit to find other pods using 8.8.8.8 as a nameserver (look for /etc/resolv.conf or dnsPolicy overrides), and pin tests to use the VPC resolver while you roll changes. If you want we can schedule a short window to help enforce the egress rules.

acme-inc: Please do. We'll schedule with you tomorrow. Thanks again for fast triage. :thumbsup:
